 Follow France brings forward minimum wage rise after mass protests
 DPA Mon, November 9, 2026 at 4:03 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. FILE PHOTO - Protesters gather at Place de la Republique during a demonstration in Paris, held as part of a nationwide day of action against the high cost of living and deteriorating conditions in schools. (is associated with: «France brings forward minimum wage rise after mass protests») Jan Schmidt-Whitley/Le Pictorium via ZUMA Press/dpa France will raise its minimum wage by 1.6% from December, bringing forward a planned increase under pressure from weeks of nationwide cost of living protests.
 Labour Minister Jean-Pierre Farandou said the hike, originally scheduled for January at a lower rate, will take effect a month early.
 He urged employers and unions to raise minimum pay rates in sector-wide collective agreements as well.
 The rise will lift the gross monthly minimum wage from around €1,867 ($2,089) to €1,897 for a 35-hour working week, an increase of nearly €30.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Farandou said the minimum wage had now risen by a total of 5.3% this year.
 Following weeks of sometimes violent demonstrations, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened talks on Monday with unions and employers' groups to discuss purchasing power and wages.
 The aim was to establish what was realistic and achievable, Lecornu said. Alongside the minimum wage increase, the government announced higher payments under a range of subsidy and support schemes.
 The CGT trade union federation dismissed the measures as "crumbs" after the talks and announced another nationwide day of strikes and protests for November 17.
